subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Should state-changing `admin-http-rpc` requests from browsers be rejected unless their origin is explicitly trusted, including in `trusted-proxy` and explicit `gateway.auth.mode="none"` deployments?
rationale: The current documentation treats the route as trusted host automation, but it also permits identity-proxy and no-auth ingress modes; deciding whether browser-origin access is supported determines whether the correct fix is shared origin enforcement, an explicit opt-in, or documentation/audit hardening.

options.title: Require Trusted Browser Origins
options.body: Reproduce the route first, then reject cross-site browser requests at the shared authenticated HTTP-route boundary while continuing to allow non-browser clients without an `Origin` header.

options.title: Preserve Trusted-Ingress Contract
options.body: Treat trusted-proxy and explicit no-auth deployments as operator-owned boundaries, adding stronger security-audit and documentation warnings rather than mandatory origin enforcement.

options.title: Add Explicit Browser Opt-In
options.body: Keep browser-origin admin HTTP requests disabled by default and permit them only through a narrowly documented origin allowlist or plugin setting.

recommendation.title: Require Trusted Browser Origins
recommendation.body: Reproduce the route first, then reject cross-site browser requests at the shared authenticated HTTP-route boundary while continuing to allow non-browser clients without an `Origin` header.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available feature-history evidence ties this person to introducing, maintaining, reviewing, and merging the affected trusted HTTP operator surface.
